body.p: By the present amendment, the claims have been amended as follows:

Claim 1 has been amended to recite that the instructions provided by the barcode include "co- ordinates of a first position of the part for attaching a first hardware component" and that the computing unit is configured to "based on the dimensions, the orientation and the co-ordinates of the first position, locate the first position of the part to provide the first hardware component".
Support for these amendments can be found throughout the application as filed, specifically at previous claim 3, paragraphs [0091] and [0094] as well as FIGs. 2-5.
Claim 3 has been cancelled.
Claim 16 has been amended to correspond with amended claim 1.

The amendments to the claims have been made without prejudice and without acquiescing to any of the Examiner's objections. Applicant reserves the right to pursue any deleted or withdrawn subject matter in a further divisional, continuation or continuation-in-part application. No new matter has been entered by the present amendment and its entry is respectfully requested/The amendments do not contain new matter and their entry is respectfully requested.

The Office Action dated November 21, 2024 (hereinafter, the "Office Action") has been carefully considered. It is believed that the amendments submitted herewith and the following comments represent a complete response to the Examiner's rejections and place the present application in condition for allowance. Reconsideration is respectfully requested.

Claims 1-10 and 12 have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Chen (U.S. 4,613,942, filed Oct. 22, 1984, hereinafter "Chen") in view of Heping (U.S. Pub. 2011/0087360, filed Mar. 30, 2009) further in view of Shinozaki (U.S. 9,649,790, filed Nov. 30, 2012, hereinafter "Shinozaki") further in view of Ross (NPL- IkeaBot: An Autonomous Multi- Robot Coordinated Furniture Assembly System, published May 2013, pgs. 855-862, hereinafter "Ross") further in view of Okuyama (U.S. Pub 2002/0105296, filed Dec. 21, 2001).

Claims 16, 20-21 and 23-28 have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Chen (U.S. 4,613,942, filed Oct. 22, 1984, hereinafter "Chen") in view of Heping (U.S. Pub. 2011/0087360, filed Mar. 30, 2009) further in view of Ross (NPL- IkeaBot: An Autonomous Multi-Robot Coordinated Furniture Assembly System, published May 2013, pgs. 855-862, hereinafter "Ross") further in view of Okuyama (U.S. Pub 2002/0105296, filed Dec. 21, 2001).
Applicant respectfully disagrees.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, as noted above, claim 1 has been amended to recite that the instructions provided by the barcode include "co-ordinates of a first position of the part for attaching a first hardware component" and that the computing unit is configured to "based on the dimensions, the orientation and the co-ordinates of the first position, locate the first position of the part to provide the first hardware component".

With regards to claim 1, Applicant notes that the Examiner asserts on page 4 of the Office Action that Chen teaches the claimed feature of "the barcode providing instructions for attaching one or more hardware components to the part to assemble the piece of furniture" at "see fig.1, numeral 14 & col. 2, lines 45-65, discloses a camera for obtaining and processing a coded indica image on a part within its field of vision. Further supporting use of a bar code for the indica in col. 4, lines 35-67. The part is then used to perform an assembly operation by the robot arm has determined by the indica outlined in col. 3, lines 25-35 & abstract".

Applicant respectfully disagrees. In addition, Applicant submits that Chen does not teach or suggest the feature of the instructions provided by the barcode including "co-ordinates of a first position of the part for attaching a first hardware component".

Applicant submits that in Chen, col. 3, lines 25-35 teaches that the "fourth set of indicia 45 comprises a series of differently colored geometric shapes, e.g., 46, 47, 48, which series identifies the operation which is to be performed by the robot arm with the part. That is, the program for the computer is on the part itself, which program instructs the robot to perform the programmed operation as set forth by the indicia. [emphasis added].

Applicant then notes that, on page 7 of the Office Action, the Examiner alleges that col. 60, lines 3-5 "discloses that the indicia provide data associated with coordinates on the part to perform the assembly instructions."
Applicant respectfully disagrees.

Col. 60, lines 3-5 of Chen state "a part having random orientation, said part having orientation indicia on said part to provide three dimensional disposition data of said part". Read in the context of the entire application, the Applicant submits that the "orientation indicia" here are shapes, specifically a red triangle and a yellow dot at one apex of the triangle. The digital image processor of Chen recognizes the triangle, and the computer measures the altitude 115 of the triangle through dot 111, as well as the rotation of the triangle about dot 111. Other differently colored dots may be disposed at the other apices.

Applicant therefore submits that, in this portion of Chen, there is no teaching of "a barcode positioned on a part presented to the robot as the part rests on a conveyor, the barcode providing instructions for attaching one or more hardware components to the part to assemble the piece of furniture, the instructions including co-ordinates of a first position of the part for attaching a first hardware component".

More generally, it is clear from the above that in Chen the indicia is scanned to instruct the robot on how to use the part that is presented with the barcode. The robot is not provided with instructions of "co-ordinates of a first position of the part" as claimed in amended claim 1.

Chen does not teach or suggest receiving any "co-ordinates of a first position of the part" that is presented to the camera because Chen is not concerned with performing operations on the part. Rather, Chen is concerned with performing operations with the part that is presented. Chen therefore does not teach that the barcode provides "co-ordinates of a first position of the part for attaching a first hardware component" because Chen is only concerned with picking up and using the parts that are presented to the camera.
For the above foregoing reasons, claim 1 as amended is novel and inventive over Chen.

With respect to the remaining prior art noted by the Examiner, Applicant further notes that in the Office Action the Examiner further asserts on page 6 that Okuyama discloses, at the Abstract and paragraphs 18, 24 and 32,

transforming the position of a moving object on the conveyer based on its coordinate system to a robot coordinate system. Further, in paragraph 8 indicating use of a camera for determining orientation and position of objects on a conveyor is known); It would have been obvious for one or ordinary skill in the art before the effective filing date of the application to have modified camera placement by mounting the camera on the robot for capturing part details and barcode data in addition to implementing known techniques for calculating parts on a conveyer based on determined coordinate systems and applying
adhesives for part assembly"
Applicant respectfully disagrees.

Okuyama does not teach or suggest the claimed step of "determining co-ordinates of a first position on the part to provide the first hardware component to the part" as alleged by the Examiner. Okuyama describes the use of a conveyor co-ordinate system to determine a position of a work on a conveyor and translate that position to a robot coordinate system. Nowhere does Okuyama teach identifying a first position on a part based on a camera capturing an image.

Further, claim 1 as amended now recites "a barcode positioned on a part presented to the robot as the part rests on a conveyor, the barcode providing instructions for attaching one or more hardware components to the part to assemble the piece of furniture, the instructions including co-ordinates of a first position of the part for attaching a first hardware component", which is also not taught in Okuyama.
Okuyama therefore does not correct the deficiencies of Chen.

Heping, Shinozaki and Ross also fail to correct the deficiencies of Chen as each reference also fails to teach or suggest at least "a barcode positioned on a part presented to the robot as the part rests on a conveyor, the barcode providing instructions for attaching one or more hardware components to the part to assemble the piece of furniture, the instructions including co-ordinates of a first position of the part for attaching a first hardware component".

Applicant therefore submits that none of the prior art cited by the Examiner teaches or suggests recites "a barcode positioned on a part presented to the robot as the part rests on a conveyor, the barcode providing instructions for attaching one or more hardware components to the part to assemble the piece of furniture, the instructions including co-ordinates of a first position of the part for attaching a first hardware component" as claimed in amended claim 1.
Therefore, claim 1 as amended is also novel and inventive over Chen in view of Heping, Shinozaki, Ross and Okuyama either alone or in combination.
Applicant submits that claims 4, 6-12 are therefore also novel and inventive over Chen in view of Shinozaki and further in view of Ross by way of their dependency on claim 1 as amended.

With respect to claims 16, 20-21 and 23-28, Applicant submits that claim 16 as amended corresponds with claim 1 as amended and therefore is novel and inventive over Chen in view of Heping, Shinozaki, Ross and Okuyama, either alone or in combination, for at least the same reasons as provided above in support of claim 1 as amended.
Claims 20-21 and 23-28 are therefore also novel and inventive over Chen in view of Heping, Shinozaki, Ross and Okuyama by way of their dependency on claim 16 as amended.

In view of the foregoing, Applicant respectfully submits that the claims, as amended, are non- obvious, and requests for this rejection under 35 U.S.C. § 103 to be withdrawn and that the claims, as amended, be allowed.

In light of Applicant's amendments to the claims and the foregoing Remarks, it is respectfully submitted that the present application is in condition for allowance. that previously pending claims are not patentable over the cited references. Rather, any alterations or characterizations are being made to facilitate expeditious prosecution of this application.
